action: Runs his hand across the solar panels, checking the readout on the van's console.
thought: Battery's full. I can breathe today.

action: Pours hot water through the filter, listening to it hum in the morning light.
thought: The sound won't leave my head.

description: While Dan confirms the barricade held and battery's full, Hui remains unsettled by the sound she heard around two on the east side.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Battery's full. Panels are clean.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I heard something last night. Around two.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Where?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: East side. Probably just wind.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Barricade held. Nothing's breached the ramp.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know. But I'm awake now.

action: Checks the solar array's connections and tightens a bolt, reads the battery status holding at ninety-six percent.
thought: Battery's holding. The rig is clean.

action: Prepares canned food and bread in the van's cab, hands moving with purpose, mind still caught on the night's sound.
thought: That sound last night. Still echoing.

description: Dan runs through the rig's wins—battery, filter, heat—while Hui dwells on last night's mystery, and they both understand the same truth: being alive beats certainty.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Battery's at ninety-six. Rig is solid.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That's good.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Filter's running. We can eat hot for once.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm still thinking about last night.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The barricade held. The ramp is still sealed.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Did it? Or did we just not hear them?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: We're still here. That's what counts.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Yeah. Yeah, we are.

action: He walks the perimeter of the solar array one last time as the light falls, checking the charge on the battery.
thought: The day held. We held.

action: She heats water on the small stove inside the van, moving with the careful quiet that darkness brings.
thought: The sound. Is it out there still?

description: Hui's lingering fear about last night's sound resists Dan's practical answers—ninety-two percent battery, a sealed ramp, nothing heard in daylight.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Ninety-two percent. The filter can run tonight.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That's good. Did you hear anything? During the day?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Nothing. Why.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Last night's sound. Still in my head.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The one in the street? Probably just the dead wandering.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Yeah. Probably.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The ramp's tight. We're sealed.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know. I know.

action: He checks the ramp's barricade as dusk darkens when Hui Ling appears with injured birds.
thought: She's going to break my rules again.

action: She carries two injured sparrows in a cloth to the van, resolved to shelter them.
thought: People died because I did nothing. Not again.

description: When Hui insists on sheltering injured birds in the van, Dan surrenders argument but holds the line—the sheltered corner, nowhere else, released by first light.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I found injured birds on the ramp. I'm bringing them up.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: That's a risk we can't carry, Hui.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know what we carry. I'm doing it anyway.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: And if noise draws them? The dead are close.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: They won't make noise. And if they do, I accept that.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You don't accept for both of us.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then I won't ask permission again. But I'm doing it.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The corner, then. Sheltered, away from the door. Gone at first light.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I'm not thanking you for this.

action: Checks the solar panel readings—77% charge, stable—and braces for what's coming.
thought: She's going to push again.

action: Heats water for tea and listens—the birds are still out there, still calling.
thought: I can't watch people die again.

description: A moral line emerges in the bird argument: Hui won't be someone who merely watches others die, and Dan's objection shows the accusation has struck.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: They're still out there.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You were outside at dawn, then.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Just listening. They need help, Dan.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: We don't know what that is. Could be fever, infection.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Or a broken wing. Something we could fix.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Once you open that door—

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Once I stop being someone who watches them die, you mean.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: That's not fair.

action: Dan stands at the van window, arms crossed, watching the battery readout as Hui Ling moves in the cab below—the argument still burning in the space between them.
thought: She won't back down. Neither can I.

action: Hui Ling sits in the van's cab, heating water on the camp stove, her movements careful and deliberate—she's not giving in, but she's also not walking out.
thought: He's afraid. More than of the dead.

description: Dan won't budge on the birds—nothing can be contained in a dead city—leaving Hui facing an impossible choice: comply with his caution or become the person who watches things die.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: We need to talk about the birds.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: There's nothing to talk about. It's not safe.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Locking out the world won't keep us alive either.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: It's kept us alive so far.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: What if I promise to be careful? To keep them contained?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You can't promise that. Nothing's contained in a dead city.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then what do you want me to do? Watch them die?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I want you safe. That's what I want.

action: He stands at the van door as the light fails, hand on the frame, listening to her shift inside among the sheltered birds.
thought: Keeping her alive means losing her.

action: She reaches for the door handle from inside the van, then stops, feeling his shadow on the other side.
thought: He's saving my life. I'm not living.

description: Hui Ling reaches for the van door as dark falls; Dan blocks the threshold, the two of them caught between the need to act and the need to survive.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm opening the door.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: It's dark. You're not.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then I release them from here.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: They'll scream. The dead will hear.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Better than this.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Better than what?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Becoming someone I don't recognize.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You recognize yourself just fine when you're alive.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Is that who we are now? Just alive?

action: He stands at the van door, blocking the way, but as Hui Ling questions him in the dark, he finally admits the truth.
thought: She's right. I can't cage her.

action: She stands at the threshold, her hand reaching for the door, and waits for his answer as the night closes in.
thought: He's afraid of losing me, not the dead.

description: At the van door in the dark, Hui Ling reaches for the handle and Dan blocks it; when she questions why, he breaks—admitting he's terrified not of the dead, but of her leaving.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm not asking to go out. I just want to open the door.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Same thing at night. Sound carries.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: They're suffering. I can hear them.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Not our problem.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Says the man who built a van to help survive. Not hide.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I built it to keep us alive. That's what matters.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Keeping alive and living aren't the same thing.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: At first light, let me open the door.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: First light, they go. That was the deal.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then why are you still blocking the door?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Because I'm afraid if I move, you will too.

action: He wakes before her and moves quietly about the van, making water for tea while the morning light spills through the window.
thought: She's leaving if I don't give something.

action: She stirs as the kettle hisses and watches him through the dawn haze, waiting.
thought: Maybe this is how he loves me.

description: Steam rises from the kettle; Dan pours tea and finally breaks the silence with a compromise — water on the ledge for the birds.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I've been thinking about the birds.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: We could set out water. On the ledge, not in here.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: They're dying, Dan. Not drinking.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know. But I don't want you going down for them. That's my line.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: So that's it. We just watch?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: No. We help them the way we can. Here.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That's not the same.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know. But it's what I can do.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then I'll do it with you.

action: Checks the solar panels—fully lit and charging—and finds Hui Ling at the van's rear window, watching the water ledge.
thought: She stops fighting when I listen.

action: Refills the water cup on the narrow ledge and watches the birds dart in and out of the gap.
thought: He finally heard me. He's trying now.

description: At the van's rear window midday, Hui Ling refills water on the ledge as birds dart in; Dan finds her there, and for once neither is braced for a fight.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The water's gone.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Good, then.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You mean it, didn't you. Last night.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: About what?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That I mattered more than the seal.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The seal doesn't matter if you're not inside it.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: So the birds stay?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The water stays. That's the deal.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That's more than water, Dan.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know.

action: Refills the water container on the van's ledge, checking the level with a thumb and watching a sparrow land to drink.
thought: She was right. This costs almost nothing.

action: Stands beside him, hands wrapped around a mug of tea, watching the birds flit in and out without flinching.
thought: He's really trying now. That matters.

description: At the van's rear in the afternoon sun, Dan refills the water dish while birds dart in unafraid; Hui Ling stands close, watching him tend it without complaint, something shifted between them.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You keep checking the level like it matters.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: It does. They'll come back if it's full.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Not what I meant.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Do you know what happens if we keep doing this? If we start caring?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: We get attached to things we can't keep. I know.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: And?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: And maybe that's the deal. We don't stop doing it anyway.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That's all I needed you to say.

action: He settles at the van door with a cup of tea, the fire warm inside.
thought: She was right. We didn't break.

action: She joins him at the door with her own cup, the city darkening beyond the ledge.
thought: The silence is soft now, not sharp.

description: Evening settles over the rooftop—the fire warm inside the van, and they settle at the door with tea as the city darkens and the birds tuck away.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You watched the birds all afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You notice everything, don't you.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Especially you. When you're thinking hard.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: About how you were right. About living.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: And?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: We can't be just careful. We have to be both.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Both scared and trying?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then we're going to be okay.

action: He settles inside the van by the fire, checking that the door is secure before sitting down beside her.
thought: She didn't leave. I opened the door.

action: She pours two cups of tea and settles by the fire, leaving space for him on the bench without pushing.
thought: He's sitting with me. That's the shift.

description: By the fire in the van, Dan and Hui Ling sit close without flinching — the city dark outside, something between them finally untensed after days of cages.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The fire's good.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah. Better than it's been.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Everything's better.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Some things. This one especially.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The birds will come back tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: They never left. Just like us.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Just like us.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I'm going to try. Keep listening.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That's all I need.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Then we're okay?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: We're getting there.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: That's enough for tonight.

action: Wakes to clear light and checks the van's power systems—batteries holding steady, the fire still warm.
thought: Clear day. Systems are solid.

action: Rises and moves to the van's rear window, looking out at the bright morning and the quiet streets below.
thought: He didn't pull the door shut last night.

description: Morning light spills through the van as they stand in the common space—Dan checking the panel readout, Hui Ling watching the bright city below and thinking about the work ahead.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Clear sky. Panels will charge fast.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Food's getting low.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I want to start a garden. Seeds, though.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I'll get seeds on the next run.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You will?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah. If you want to do it, I'm in.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Okay. Thank you, Dan.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Don't thank me. Just grow something.

action: At the garden corner in the clear sun, Dan listens as Hui Ling outlines the planter expansion, then gathers wood and tools to build the new beds.
thought: She sees clearer than I do. I'm learning.

action: Seeing the food at seven days, Hui Ling moves to the garden corner and proposes a clear plan to expand the planter beds, then pulls Dan in to help build.
thought: He heard me the first time. That's new.

description: With the food down to seven days, Hui Ling pitches a garden expansion at the garden corner in the bright sun; Dan listens without resistance and by midday they're building a new planter bed frame together, her planning and his hands aligned.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Food's down to seven days. We need more plants.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The garden's producing.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Not fast enough. Help me expand it today?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You've already planned it.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Double the corner planter. I can manage it with your help.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Okay. Where do we start?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Corner bed. More space, better soil.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Then let's build it.

action: He stands beside Hui Ling at the corner bed, handing her the seedling tray and tools as she directs the spacing of the first seeds.
thought: She sees clearer than I do.

action: She kneels at the corner bed, turning the soil and beginning to space the first seeds, her hands steady in the afternoon light as Dan watches without pushing back.
thought: He's stepping back. That's everything.

description: In the bright afternoon, Hui Ling works the corner bed while Dan stands beside her, handing seeds and soil—watching her lead, his hands serving her vision for the first time.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: We should plant before the week's out. You with me?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Those seeds are old. Might not take.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then they're stubborn. Maybe they'll surprise us.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: What layout are you thinking?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Corner bed first. You turn soil, I'll space the seeds.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Not the other way?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I need to see it as we go.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Then that's how we do it.

action: He checks the battery readout by the fire, listening to the city darkening outside.
thought: Maybe seeing further matters more than control.

action: She watches the windows fade from orange to purple, then turns to him with the first honest question.
thought: He came around. What does that mean tomorrow?

description: By the fire in the van as evening settles, with food now at five days, Dan asks about the garden's timeline—she feels him taking her vision seriously.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Five days if we're careful. We need to think about a run soon.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The garden beds you started—how long before they're producing?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Three weeks at minimum. Four if it's slow.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Then we go by day six. I'll take it.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Alone again?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Safer. You hold the deck.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I didn't like it last time.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know you didn't.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Come back.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I will.

action: He checks the battery readout and pulls the radio forward, preparing to keep her in contact tomorrow.
thought: I'm letting her walk into the dead.

action: She empties a satchel and lays out what she'll need for the morning run into the city.
thought: Tomorrow I feed us both. I have to.

description: Inside the van at night, with three days of food left, Hui Ling decides she'll scavenge tomorrow—and Dan, struggling, finally says yes.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Three days of food.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: We ration harder.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Someone has to scavenge tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I'll go. Clear morning.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm going.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: No. Too risky.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You don't trust me?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I'm scared.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: So am I. But I'm going.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Okay. Take the radio.

action: He fills two flasks at the water rig and hands them to Hui Ling at the van door, watching her check her blade.
thought: She walks toward the dead, and I let her.

action: She checks her blade at the van door, shoulders her pack, and takes the flasks from Dan—ready to head into the streets.
thought: Two days of food. I have to try.

description: Clear morning, perfect for scavenging—Hui Ling shoulders her pack at the van door while Dan hands over the filled flasks, their goodbye loaded with words left unspoken.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Clear morning—best light for scavenging we've had.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You have the route?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Corner shops, quick, back in two hours.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Radio charged?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Charged. You'll hear me if I need you.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Hui Ling.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know. I'm coming back.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Every time?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Every time. That's the deal between us.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Then go.

action: He steps out to meet her as she climbs the ramp, hands checking her over before pulling her close.
thought: Fear breaks into something softer now.

action: She comes up the ramp with her pack heavy, breathing hard but steady, ready to show him what she found.
thought: He believed I could do it. I did.

description: Hui Ling returns from the streets below with supplies in her pack; Dan meets her at the van door, checking her over before they sit together sorting through what she found.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Found a pharmacy three streets over, mostly picked. We have food.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You're okay?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Fine. And there was medicine on one shelf, still sealed.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: How much total?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Two days of food, some antibiotics. It worked, Dan.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You did good. Really good.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I was scared the whole time. But I knew I could do it.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I knew you could. I was just scared you wouldn't come back.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm back. We're okay now.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah. We're okay.

action: He settles by the fire as Hui Ling spreads the pharmacy supplies, checking each item.
thought: She made it. She's really back.

action: She arranges the pharmacy supplies on a cloth, precise and careful, weariness showing at the edges.
thought: Food in our hands. Fear in mine.

description: Hui Ling spreads the pharmacy haul—tins, dried goods, fruit—by the fire while Dan joins her; the relief of her return and the weight of what she saw shape the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: There's tinned fruit. Real fruit.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Where did you find that?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Basement of the old pharmacy, two blocks south. The storeroom was sealed.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Two blocks. That's—

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I marked the route. No dead around the building.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You came back. That's what matters.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I saw someone on the way back. Woman with a bitten arm.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You couldn't reach her.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: No. But we have food now. We have time.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Eat with me while it's warm?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Yeah. Let's.

action: He tends the fire, warming the evening meal from Hui Ling's haul, watching her carefully as she begins to speak about the streets below.
thought: She came back and I let her.

action: She settles by the fire, spreading the tins and supplies across the deck, her triumph mixing with something she's struggling not to carry alone.
thought: I made it back. Can't unsee her arm.

description: By the fire as dusk held, Hui Ling spreads the pharmacy haul while Dan tends the flames, their conversation moving from her triumph to the weight she carried back from the streets below.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The pharmacy haul alone could stretch us weeks.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You came back whole. That's what matters.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: My hands were shaking the entire way down.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: But you kept moving. Came back with this.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: There was a woman down there. Bitten arm.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: How close? Did she see you?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Two blocks away. She didn't see me.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Then sit. Eat. You're safe now.

action: He sits beside her by the fire, listening while she speaks about the woman with the bitten arm, not offering solutions or consolation.
thought: She's carrying more than I measured for.

action: She sits close to the fire, telling Dan for the first time about the woman she had to leave behind, her hands still trembling.
thought: I saved us. It doesn't feel like saving.

description: By the fire in the van, Hui Ling finally tells Dan about the bitten woman she passed; he listens without consoling, and she grieves the impossible choice that kept them both alive.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: There was a woman. Three blocks past. Bitten arm.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You didn't stop.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: If I had, I wouldn't have come back.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: That's what saved us both.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Her eyes, Dan. She knew I was leaving her there.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I'm sorry you had to see that.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Am I still nursing if I walk past the dying?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You were never going to save her. But you saved us.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Feels like I chose myself over her life.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You chose both of us. That's the whole thing—you couldn't have both.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: How do you live with that? The impossible choices?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: One night at a time. Stop thinking past tomorrow.

action: Dan stirs the fire and pours tea for both of them, waiting for her to speak.
thought: She knows what she needs; I just listen.

action: Hui Ling wraps her hands around the warm cup and lets the quiet settle between them.
thought: Yesterday happened. I came back anyway.

description: The woman from yesterday haunts Hui Ling's morning, but she's steady; Dan brings tea and sits by the fire, just listening and following her lead as they plan the day.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: How'd you sleep?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Off and on. Kept replaying yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The good part or the hard part?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Both. The woman's arm — I can't unsee it.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: But you came back. You did what we needed.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I did. It doesn't feel like it yet.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: What would help?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Checking the garden. Making sure things are growing, not dying.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Let's do that.

action: Spreads the last of the fresh food from yesterday's haul and begins sorting it by shelf life, working slow and methodical.
thought: Can't stop seeing that arm.

action: Joins her by the fire, watching her sort, his hands idle but ready, just following her lead.
thought: She's carrying more than the haul.

description: By midday, they sort the pharmacy haul by the fire — Hui Ling quieter than yesterday, Dan present and steady, not pushing, trusting her with the weight she carries.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Fruit first. Everything else after.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You sleep okay?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Not really.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: There was a woman with a bitten arm.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: And you still came back.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: We needed the food more.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You did what you had to.

action: He tends the fire while Hui Ling sorts the pharmacy haul by its warmth.
thought: Not fighting her. That's new.

action: She sorts the pharmacy haul by the fire, steady-handed despite yesterday's pull.
thought: He's trusting me. Really trusting.

description: Food runs out in two days. By the fire in the van, they plan the next run—Hui Ling resting first, Dan holding the ramp.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Food's gone in two days.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I can go tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: What do you need?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: A day. Sleep, and to not think about yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Then we take a day.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You could come with me.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Someone has to keep the ramp.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Yeah. I know.

action: He sits by the fire, helping her repack without argument, his hands steady though his face is tight.
thought: She's stronger than I am. Accepting that.

action: She lays out tomorrow's gear by the fire, speaking the route aloud, watching his face for the fight that doesn't come.
thought: He's really letting me go this time.

description: By evening with food at three days, they sit by the fire naming tomorrow's run aloud—Hui Ling steady, Dan finally letting her lead.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Tomorrow. I'm going tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: South?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Hospital district. It still has what we need.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Riskier. More dead that way now.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Everywhere's risky now.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: And you're still letting me go.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I am.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I wasn't sure you would.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Neither was I. But you know what you're doing.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Help me check the pack, then?

action: Sits by the fire in the van, listening as Hui Ling names what haunts her, his hands steady on his knees instead of reaching to fix or turn away.
thought: Serving her vision is simpler than I thought.

action: Sits across from him by the fire, naming the bitten arm that won't leave her mind, but stays steady in the knowledge that he's listening without turning away.
thought: He's holding the line with me, not for me.

description: By nightfall, Hui Ling is haunted by yesterday's bitten woman—her arm won't leave—but Dan sits by the fire listening without turning away, learning to hold the weight with her instead of sealing them against it.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That arm keeps coming back.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I don't know how to stop seeing it.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You don't have to.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Tomorrow I go back out there.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You do what you need to do.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: And you hold the ramp.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Always.

action: He wakes early and sits by the fire, checking the empty food stores while waiting for her.
thought: The food's gone. Time to let her go.

action: She wakes haunted by yesterday's bitten arm but joins him by the fire, steady to plan the run.
thought: That woman's arm haunts me. But I'll go.

description: One tin remains; Hui Ling wakes haunted but resolves to run again, and Dan sits by the fire steady, learning not to seal them in.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You're quiet this morning.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Couldn't stop seeing that woman's arm.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know. You don't have to go today.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: One tin. I have to.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Eat first. Then go careful.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I will. Where should I look?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Apartments three blocks east. Should be untouched stock.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'll move fast. Back before dark.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You will be. I'm holding the ramp.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You're trusting me.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah. I am.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Don't let me lose myself out there.

action: Dan packs her supplies, hands over the rope, and positions himself at the ramp block—holding steady while she heads for the ledge.
thought: She trusts me to hold steady.

action: Hui Ling shoulders the supplies and makes for the rooftop edge, carrying yesterday's haunting with her into the city.
thought: The arm won't let me forget.

description: With one tin left and daylight burning, Hui Ling prepares to run while Dan steadies her—no fighting it now, just the weight they share.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm going to move now. While I'm steady.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Okay. Same routes as yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Pharmacy on the south side. If it's still there.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Full flask, the rope, whistle if the ramp needs you.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That woman's arm won't leave me.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You did what you could. That's all.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Is it enough?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You come back, and we figure out the rest.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I won't be long.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I'll be at the ramp.

action: He checks the barricaded ramp one final time, running his hands over the reinforcement, listening for any sound from below.
thought: Let her go. She's stronger than me.

action: She fills three water flasks from the tank, checks the straps on her pack, and shoulders it with the last tin inside.
thought: The arm is still there. Go anyway.

description: With the last tin packed and power steady, Hui Ling gears up at the barricaded ramp for the afternoon run.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: One tin left.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Flasks full?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Yeah. Filter's clean. I'm ready.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Pharmacy, then clinic, back?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That's the plan.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Two hours max.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The arm from yesterday—it's still there.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Every time I close my eyes.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: And you're going anyway.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: We don't eat otherwise.

action: He heard her at the ramp and went down to meet her, carrying the supplies back as she climbed into the van to rest.
thought: She made it back alive.

action: She collapsed by the fire with exhaustion and relief, the haunting weight of the arm she couldn't save still pressing against her mind.
thought: The arm's still there. But so is he.

description: She returned from the scavenge with tins to stretch their days and a haunting she couldn't leave behind; by evening Dan was holding that weight with her, both warming by the fire as darkness claimed the city below.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I found four days, maybe. Pharmacy two blocks over.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You hurt?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: No. But when I came back up, she was still there—that arm, Dan, it was just—

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You made it back. That's what matters now.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Is it? She didn't.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You can't carry that up here.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I can't stop carrying it.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Then I'll carry it with you.

action: He builds up the fire and sits beside her in the van's rear, listening to the night press against the barricade.
thought: She came back. I can hold this.

action: She watches the flames while speaking the day's horror aloud, naming the arm and the fear, and lets him sit with both.
thought: He's not turning away from it.

description: By the fire in the van's rear, Hui Ling names the severed arm haunting her from the dead streets while Dan sits beside her without flinching; three tins sit packed in the storage corner, a mercy and a question about how long it will last.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The arm won't stop being there, even when I close my eyes.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know. You did good today.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I should have to live with that. I chose to go.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Three tins bought us maybe five more days.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: If that's all we've got, I'll go again.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Not for a few days. Rest first.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Okay. Thank you for letting me go.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Thank you for coming back.

action: He poured hot water for tea and laid out the day's rations, watching her face across the van's rear table.
thought: She's steady. I can release my grip.

action: She sipped the tea slowly, checking her pack and her hands—preparing for the run without the old dread now.
thought: The arm is still there. So is he.

description: Morning sun charges the panels; Dan steadies Hui Ling with tea while she preps for a run, the haunting still present but no longer keeping her paralyzed.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Sun's good. The panels are climbing already.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You slept. That matters.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You were holding steady beside me. That's why.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The tins are holding?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Four days, maybe five if we're careful. Enough to run again.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You want to go?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Yeah. The arm's still there, but I can move through it now.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I'll check the ramp. Gate stays solid.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know. That's why I can go.

action: He's sorting through tomorrow's pack, counting the tins with methodical precision, his focus absolute.
thought: I can't hold her and survive.

action: She watches the pile of supplies, her mind already mapping the streets below: how far to push, where to look first.
thought: The fear doesn't stop the needing.

description: With food down to three tins, they finalize tomorrow's run at the storage corner—Dan afraid but asking what she needs, Hui Ling steady and clear.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: South again, or should we push further?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: South's pretty clean now. Further means hours out.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Three tins won't stretch anymore.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: How far would you go?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: As far as I need to find something.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: And if you don't find anything?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then I keep looking.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Okay. I believe you.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You're really okay with this?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I'm terrified. But I'm okay with it.

action: He checks the solar battery meter and her pack knots, moving between them like one confirms the other will hold.
thought: I can't control her. Only myself.

action: She sorts the rations into her pack and pulls the light rope from storage, moving with the calm of someone who has decided.
thought: His fear is how he loves me.

description: Clear sun charged the battery all morning; by afternoon Hui Ling was sorting supplies at the storage corner while Dan checked her rope and knots, both quiet with the weight of tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The pack's ready. Light rope, full load.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: How far down the grid?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Far enough to count. Not far enough to get trapped.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: That's still vague.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Because I don't know yet. Won't know until I'm moving.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Then let's get the battery to full before you go.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: It's fine now.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: It's better full. And it keeps my hands busy.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Fair.

action: Sits by the fire in the van's rear, watching Hui Ling's pack and the rope coiled by the door, listening to the city beyond the barricade.
thought: She's ready. I'm not holding her back.

action: Finishes her meal by firelight, running through tomorrow's route in her head, the pack at the door holding her plan.
thought: He's letting me go. That changes everything.

description: Battery full from a clear day; Dan and Hui Ling sit by the fire in the van's rear, her pack ready by the door, tomorrow's run hours away.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Pack's by the door. Rope's set.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm going to sleep soon. Need to be sharp.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Eat a bit more before you sleep.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: We should save it for after.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You won't come back light. Just eat.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Okay.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: And tie the rope twice if you find anything.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I will, Dan.

action: Dan checked Hui Ling's rope and pack one final time, then sat beside her by the fire.
thought: Fear fades when I stop holding on.

action: Hui Ling rested by the fire, pack ready by the door, while Dan sat close without words needed.
thought: Ready now, and he won't hold back.

description: Dan checked the rope one final time while Hui Ling rested by the fire in the van's rear; both quiet and ready, her pack set by the door for tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You've checked that rope seven times.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Eight. I wasn't keeping count.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: And?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: It's perfect. You're ready.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: So why keep checking?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Because I'm scared of losing you.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: But you're letting me go anyway.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah. Because you need to. I'm done holding on.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: That's new.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Everything's new now.

action: He sits by the fire checking her rope one last time, hands slow and careful.
thought: If I let go, we both survive this.

action: She eats the last tin slowly, watching him work, pack ready by the door.
thought: He's scared. He's letting me go anyway.

description: By the fire in the van's rear, they split the last tin; she eats and he checks her rope, pack ready by the door, knowing she goes this morning.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The rope's set.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I checked every knot three times.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I watched you check twice.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Come back.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Always.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Two hours down?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Down and back the same, three if I find something good.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The pharmacy first.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then the clinic if it sounds clear.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Don't go in alone if you hear them.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know the signs.

action: He stood at the ramp barricade as she disappeared into the street, listening for movement, rope gripped tight against any sign of the dead rising.
thought: I'm terrified. I trust her anyway.

action: She descended into the dead city moving west, searching the apartment blocks for food and medicine, the rope secure and the van at her back.
thought: The dead won't stop me. I'm ready.

description: The food tin was scraped clean this morning; by midday she was at the ramp with her pack ready, and he checked her rope one last time, quiet and steady, before she dropped into the dead city.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Food's gone. I'm going down today.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah. West is clear.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: How long do I have?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Six hours before dark. You've done harder.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The dead?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Quiet this morning. Stick to the alleys.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I will.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Come back whole.

action: He waited at the ramp all afternoon, watching the empty streets below until she climbed back up with the cans.
thought: I wanted to order her back. I didn't.

action: She made it back from the picked-clean streets with two cans and the strange quiet of the dead city still in her ears.
thought: He was terrified. He let me choose.

description: She came back from the run with two cans; Dan had waited at the ramp, and they sat by the fire in the van, the food crisis now impossible to ignore.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I found two cans. The rest was picked clean.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You're okay?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Yeah. Streets were empty. The dead weren't out.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: How long?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Three hours, maybe. Lost track.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Three hours.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I came back. I'm back.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know. I'm learning.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You didn't tell me not to go.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I wanted to. God, I wanted to.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: But you didn't.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: No.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: So we eat tonight. I'll go again if I have to.

action: He sits by the fire, listening to her describe what she saw below, quiet and steady as she speaks.
thought: She's processing it, not breaking.

action: She settles by the fire, describing the uncanny silence of the streets and the doll she found, watching his face as she speaks.
thought: The doll won't leave my head.

description: By the fire's glow, she tells him about the silence and the doll on the pavement; Dan listens, counts the food they brought back, and says nothing about the run after tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The city felt wrong today. Too quiet.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Quiet means they didn't see you.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I found a doll on the curb. A child's toy, just... sitting there.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You can't carry every ghost in this city.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm not trying to. But I saw it.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You came back safe with food. That's the whole thing.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: One tin left after tonight.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: We've done more with less before.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Another run soon, then.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: We'll manage it.

action: He sits by the fire in the van's rear, listening to her speak of the doll without offering solution or reassurance.
thought: I couldn't fix it, but I could sit.

action: By the fire, she breaks the silence and speaks of the doll on the pavement, and he listens instead of trying to erase what she carried back.
thought: He heard me and didn't look away.

description: By the fire in the van's rear, the last tin gone, Hui Ling speaks what haunts her—a doll on the pavement—and Dan sits with her grief instead of trying to fix it.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I keep seeing that doll's face when I close my eyes.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: There was a child. I don't know how long ago.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You're here. That matters.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Does it? I came back with food and left that child there.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You came back alive. That's what had to happen.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know. Doesn't make the doll any less small.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: No. But you carried it anyway. That's the difference.

action: Checks the solar panels in the clear morning light, then walks to the ramp where Hui Ling is gearing up her pack, and stands beside the barricade without blocking her.
thought: She's leaving and I'm not stopping her.

action: Wakes with the sun, checks what little food remains, and begins packing her scavenging bag by the ramp with careful, practiced movements.
thought: The doll's still there. I have to go.

description: Stores empty, sun climbing; Hui Ling is packed at the ramp and Dan stands beside her without blocking the way.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: We've got nothing left.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Panels are charging good. You ready?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'll go. Sun's high, visibility's clear.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Same route as yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Different streets. More careful this time.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know you will.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You're really okay with this?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: No. But I'm doing it anyway.

action: Loading her pack with steady hands, each choice a refusal to hold her back.
thought: She's leaving. I can't stop her.

action: Shouldering the pack at the ramp, eyes on the empty streets below.
thought: He's terrified. He's letting me anyway.

description: At the ramp's barricade, Dan loads her pack one last time while Hui Ling waits—the food gone, the streets empty, the choice finally made.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The pharmacy's four blocks out. It'll still be full.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Four blocks from here. Two from where they cluster.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I've mapped the route. I'll move fast.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know you will. That's not why I'm scared.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then what?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Losing you. But I'm not holding you back.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'll be back by dark.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Alive is all I need. The food doesn't matter.

action: He watches her check the rope one last time, then steps back from the barricade.
thought: She's leaving and I'm not stopping her.

action: She tests the rope tied to the ramp, adjusts her pack, and begins the careful descent toward the streets below.
thought: Down there, the doll. I have to go.

description: At the ramp in the bright afternoon, Hui Ling checks her rope one last time while Dan watches without blocking her path—both silent, knowing this is it, the food gone and the city empty below.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The rope's secure?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Tested it twice. You have water?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Two bottles and the knife.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Fifth is clear, but stay away from the shadows.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know the route. Back by dark.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Just come back.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The doll—I saw it from the edge yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know. Go.

action: Watched the empty streets all afternoon, then pulled the rope hand over hand as she climbed the ramp wall in the dusk.
thought: She came back alive.

action: Descended into the dead city, found the pharmacy with food and the doll, and climbed back toward his waiting hands as the sun fell.
thought: He was there waiting.

description: As dusk fell, Hui Ling climbed the ramp wall on Dan's rope while streets grew dark below; by night, the doll and three tins lay on the van table between them.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I see you. Move.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm climbing.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I've got the rope.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Three tins from the pharmacy.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You're clear.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The doll was still there.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You were right to go.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: So were you, to let me.

action: He settles by the fire, shoulders finally loose, as Hui Ling closes the van door and leans against him.
thought: She's here. She's alive. I can breathe.

action: She closes the van door and settles beside Dan, the doll and three tins on the table glowing in the firelight beside them.
thought: He let me go. He actually trusted me.

description: She came back with the doll and food while Dan kept watch; now they're in the van, the fire burning warm, both learning a new way to hold on.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The doll's safe now.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You're safe now. That matters more.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know. And you let me go.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I wasn't sure I could.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I knew you could. That's why I went.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I was terrified. Still am.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I know. But you held the rope.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Come sit. Let me hold you instead.

action: Pours hot water for coffee from the heated tank, watching Hui Ling fold water canisters by the fire without interfering in her system.
thought: She's choosing this. I don't have to manage it.

action: Organizes the water canisters and filter materials with care, aware of Dan moving quietly beside her without hovering or correcting her arrangement.
thought: He's not watching like I'll disappear.

description: Clear dawn in the van; the battery is full, the fire warm, and Dan pours coffee while Hui Ling arranges the water stores—trust earned yesterday becoming routine.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Listen. It's quiet. Real quiet, no moaning.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Weather held. Panels charging hard.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Then we can run hot water all morning.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Run it as long as you need. What's your order?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: My order? Since when do you ask?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Since you came back alive and nothing broke.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Nothing broke. That's the whole day, isn't it.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Seems like it. One day at a time.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Yeah. One day at a time.

action: Sits on a low edge near the garden, watching the rooftop and the city beyond while Hui Ling kneels in the soil.
thought: I can sit still and not lose her.

action: Kneels in the rooftop garden, planting seeds and checking the soil depth, aware of Dan's steady presence nearby.
thought: He's finally not counting the time.

description: Hui Ling tends the rooftop garden while Dan sits on a nearby ledge, and the silence between them is easy for the first time — no clock-watching, no fear, just two people at their own work.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: The garden's taking. The soil's rich.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You've got the depth right. Good work.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I thought it would fail. Everything else did.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Most things don't make it. But some do.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm betting on that. For the seeds, for us.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know. I'm not fighting it anymore.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: What changed?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You came back yesterday. That was enough.

action: He discovers the solar array frame has collapsed and moves through the wreckage, checking which panels are salvageable and which connections are severed.
thought: I can fix this. Just need the materials.

action: She finds Dan at the collapsed rig and moves with him through the debris, understanding at once what has to happen—and that she will be the one to go.
thought: He's trusting me. I won't let him down.

description: The solar rig fails in the afternoon wind; Dan and Hui Ling stand at the collapsed frame, checking which panels are salvageable and planning the rebuild.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The rig's gone. Frame's destroyed.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: What happened?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Wind, I think. The mounts weren't strong enough.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Can you rebuild?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah. Need metal, bolts, brackets.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'll get them.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: It'll be in the city. Dangerous.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I've done it before.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I know. Tomorrow, then.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: At dawn.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: I'll have the ramp locked.

action: Stands at the collapsed solar array frame in the cooling evening, running hands over bent metal and cracked panels, already calculating salvage points.
thought: Frame bends but doesn't break. We're okay.

action: Kneels beside the array turning over a cracked panel, checking if cells inside are salvageable, tracking Dan's assessment with quiet focus.
thought: He's not spiraling, and neither am I.

description: By the damaged solar array in the cooling evening, Dan and Hui Ling stand assessing what the afternoon wind broke—two cracked panels, a bent frame—already planning salvage and tomorrow's rebuild.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Two panels cracked, one frame bent. Could've been worse.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Frame's fixable. Panels… we're down to three working.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: What about the battery? It held the wind.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Held. Frame caught the worst. We lost mounting points.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: So we rebuild the mounts and salvage what we can?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah. That's the job.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Okay. We'll do that tomorrow when it's light.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You're steady about this.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: We're steady about this.

action: Lay out the damaged panel pieces and the bent solar frame on the deck, accounting for what's salvageable and what's lost.
thought: The tools are there. I can fix this.

action: Check the frame's bend and test each cracked panel, helping Dan separate what can be straightened from what's truly gone.
thought: He's not falling apart. We've got this.

description: By the van's light, Dan lays out salvageable panel pieces while Hui Ling checks the frame's bend—no panic, just accounting for what broke and what can still work.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Two panels are gone, but the frame is just bent.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Can you straighten it?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: The torch and some weight, maybe three hours tomorrow if it's clear.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You'll want help?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Your hands are steadier. Spot me on the rig?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Of course.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: This isn't the end of it.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: No. But we've handled worse.

action: He kneels at the solar array, checking the bent frame with his hands, testing its flex, and laying out the cracked panels.
thought: Frame bends but doesn't break. Spares ready.

action: She emerges from the van with water and settles beside him at the array, checking the damage with quiet hands.
thought: He's not panicking. Just building again.

description: In the early light, Dan checks the bent frame and cracked panels at the solar array while Hui Ling sits with water—bad damage but spares ready, both steady.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: You're already working?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Frame's bent, two panels cracked.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Can you fix it?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Have spares in storage. Planned for this.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Of course you did.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Come help me get them out?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Yeah. Let's get the rig back online.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Shouldn't take long.

action: He kneels among the salvageable panels, assessing which breaks can be patched and which parts are gone.
thought: Most of it we can fix.

action: She sits nearby watching the dead city below, hands on her knees, present but quietly thinking further ahead.
thought: We can't just keep patching things.

description: In clear midday, Dan and Hui Ling sort yesterday's wind damage—salvageable panels and bent frame—their hands steady but a question rising: whether this roof can hold them both much longer.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: How many days do we have without panels?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Three, maybe four if we run minimal.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: And if we can't salvage these?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Then we've got maybe two months before power becomes the problem.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: Not if we move sooner.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Move where?

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I don't know yet. Somewhere with more options.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Options mean risk.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: So does staying.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Yeah.

action: Dan kneels by the cracked panels at the solar array, assessing what the wind left salvageable and what can't be fixed again.
thought: I finally admitted: I don't know the answers.

action: Hui Ling sits on a tool crate, watching him work, then finally says aloud what they've both been thinking.
thought: He trusted me enough to doubt. That's new.

description: At the solar array, Dan and Hui Ling stand over cracked panels and a bent frame, and Dan finally says aloud what Hui Ling's been thinking: they can't keep doing this.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: It held.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: This time.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: We can patch the next time.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: How many times, though?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: As many as it takes.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: But we're still just surviving.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: Surviving is what matters.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: For how long, like this?

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: You're saying we leave.

dialogue.speaker: huiling
dialogue.line: I'm saying we should think about it.

dialogue.speaker: dan
dialogue.line: And maybe we should.
